newsitem.title: UK: Bell Lines rescue deadline extended to July 5.
newsitem.headline: Bell Lines rescue deadline extended to July 5.

text.p: The deadline for agreeing restructuring plans for troubled Irish short sea shipping operator Bell Lines has been extended to July 5, a spokesman for the company said Tuesday.
Bell Lines receiver David Hughes of Ernst and Young had been due to present plans to the Dublin High Court today.

A spokesman for Hughes, who was not available, said an adjournment to the court hearing had been granted and the deadline has been extended to July 5. More time was needed to consider certain aspects of the plans, he added.
He said a consortium comprising the Irish Agricultural Wholesale Society, ACT Venture Capital and Dublin-based ports and transport group Imari have proposed a rescue plan for Bell Lines.
They are proposing to inject between three and five million punt cash into the company.

A previous consortium including Irish Continental Group, NatWest Venture Capital and Citycorp Venture Capital, which together owned 85 percent of Bell Lines, pulled out of a proposed three million punt rescue package at the beginning of June due to opposition from some creditors.
Opposition came mainly from Waterford Harbour Commissioners and the Ministry for Marine which would have acted as guarantor of the port's debts.

Bell Lines, which has trading debts of around 20 million punt, ran into difficulties in 1995 and 1996 mainly due to a freight price war on the North Sea and competition from the Channel Tunnel. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
